newsitem.title: UK: Dalgety to halve investment in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dalgety to halve investment in 1997.

text.p: British food company Dalgety Plc will reduce its capital expenditure this year by almost half to about 75 million stg now that all its major projects are completed, finance director John Martyn said on Monday.
The company has invested heavily over the last two years on new food ingredient factories at Portbury in south west England Portbury, Wittstock in Germany and Standon in Hertfordshire.
Net debt increased to 305 million stg from 281 million stg, giving a gearing ratio of 76 percent, as at December 31, 1996. "We should now see a declining trend in gearing," Martyn told reporters.
The export ban on British beef in April 1996 also meant Dalgety incurred reorganisation costs of 47 million stg on its pet food business.
